subject: Post-call: starter discount path + 1M-token unit economics
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: starter discount path + 1M-token unit economics

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we discussed on the call.

Summary of what Brightline needs (as I heard it):
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + customer message routing for support flows (aggregate sequence lengths ~300 tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~200M tokens/month in Q1 of production; spiky in first 3 months as we ramp.
- Initial pilot: 10M–25M tokens over 30 days to validate latency and quality.
- Security: SOC2 acceptable; would need audit logs retained for 12 months.

Pricing & asks from your side:
- Target unit economics: ~$800–1,200 per 1M tokens for the pilot to hit your budget band.
- Interest in a starter discount (startup program) and an option to convert to a committed use discount for 12–24 month term if the pilot metrics look good.

Proposed next steps (agreed on call):
1) I’ll send a starter pricing sketch (attached) that shows: baseline hosted rate, starter startup discount, and committed-use pathing with example 12/24mo tiered % discounts.
2) You’ll share the usage snapshot (you indicated you could export a 3-month dev/staging sample) — attach that reply so I can run a quick model.
3) If the starter pricing looks OK, we’ll put a pilot order on a short DocuSign that gives you the startup credits/discount and a 60-day option to convert to committed pricing.

Attachments: [Attachment: RI-pricing-proposal-Brightline.pdf (PDF, 78KB)] [Attachment: Brightline-usage-snapshot.csv (CSV, 14KB) — TBD by Tom]

Questions for you now: can you confirm the pilot budget band (target $/1M token you referenced) and whether legal needs an initial MSA redline before DocuSign?

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Monica on approval guidance internally once you confirm the budget band.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@brightline.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: starter discount path + 1M-token unit economics

Thanks Laura — appreciate the recap.

Confirmed items:
- Pilot budget band: our finance lead gave a hard cap of $1,000 per 1M tokens for the pilot (so 10M tokens would be $10k for the month at target).
- Pilot target: 10–20M tokens first month, then expect to hit 150–200M tokens/mo by month 3 if latency/quality are good.
- We will need 12 months of audit logs; SOC2 + CP section is a must.

Legal: we prefer not to run a full MSA redline for the starter pilot — if you can provide the DocuSign starter order that references your standard MSA and provides 30 days to review, that should be fine.

I’m attaching the 90-day usage export (dev + staging) as discussed — highlights: most requests are <400 tokens, median 220 tokens.

Best,
Tom

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: starter discount path + 1M-token unit economics

Forwarding Tom’s email + usage snapshot. Key asks: starter discount to hit $1,000/1M token for the pilot (10–20M month-1), and ability to convert to a committed 12–24mo discount once they ramp to 150–200M tokens/month.

Questions for pricing/approval:
- Can we offer a startup/starter discount that nets them ~$1,000 per 1M for the first 30–60 days? If so, what signals should we require (e.g., payment method on file, signed starter order, usage guardrails)?
- If they convert to committed-use, what are recommended discount tiers for 12mo vs 24mo at ~200M tokens/mo steady state? (include an example $/1M and total committed spend).
- Do we need Finance/RevOps to pre-approve the DocuSign template or can we use the standard starter order?

I think there’s a real upside here given the ramp profile — Tom was explicit about converting if latency/quality hold. Looking for a quick internal decision so I can return to Tom today.

—Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: starter discount path + 1M-token unit economics

Thanks for the context — looks promising. My recommended approach:

1) Starter order (pilot):
- Offer a 30-day starter discount that targets $1,000 / 1M tokens.
- Requirements: payment method on file + signed starter order (DocuSign), usage cap set at 25M tokens for the 30-day pilot.
- Legal: use standard starter order (no MSA redline). Finance OKs the small credit hold; RevOps will sanity-check billing metadata (project id + invoice code).

2) Committed conversion (if they ramp to >=150M tokens/mo within 90 days):
- 12-month commitment at 150M tokens/mo: propose 20% off baseline hosted list -> example $/1M = $800 (illustrative).
- 24-month commitment at 200M tokens/mo: propose 30% off baseline -> example $/1M = $700.
- Include an automatic true-up monthly clause for overages; commit bands apply to committed base only.

3) Approvals & docs:
- RevOps: will need the deal metadata before DocuSign (I’ll loop them with the HubSpot deal id).
- Discounts at the 30% level need Director approval — I can sign off if Legal and RevOps grade are clean.

Laura — you can respond to Tom with the starter order and the 30-day cap; I’ll prep the committed-use examples and a short one-page summary for Finance to pre-approve.

Ben Carter
Head of Growth — SMB & Startups | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: RI-commit-conversion-examples.xlsx (XLSX, 32KB)]
